Reference points of a proximity test

Source: R/reference.R
reference_points.Rd

Returns the points a proximity test measures distance to: capitals, country and province centroids, biodiversity institutions, the GBIF headquarters, or the points of the Artificial Hotspot Occurrence Inventory (Park et al. 2023). The table can be inspected, filtered or extended and passed back through the gazetteers argument of flag_occurrences().

Usage

reference_points(
  test = c("capital", "centroid", "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "aohi"),
  reference = c("natural_earth", "CoordinateCleaner")
)

Arguments

test

One of "capital", "centroid", "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "aohi".

reference

"natural_earth" (the package's own gazetteers) or "CoordinateCleaner" (that package's tables, which must be installed).

Value

A data frame with columns lon and lat and, for the package's own gazetteers, the attributes of each point: name, country, adm0_a3, iso_a2, class for capitals; name, adm0_a3, code, type, method for centroids; key, code, name, country, city, type, active, master_source for institutions (GRSciColl); id, taxon (the group the hotspot was found in: Aves, Insecta, Mammalia, Plantae), frequency (records at the point), category, determination (TRUE for a real observation site, FALSE for an artificial aggregate of records) and notes for the inventory. For reference = "CoordinateCleaner" the columns are lon and lat only.

Examples

head(reference_points("capital"))
table(reference_points("centroid")$type)
